newsitem.title: USA: Most U.S. debt futures end quiet range trade lower.
newsitem.headline: Most U.S. debt futures end quiet range trade lower.

text.p: Most U.S. debt futures ended a session of uneventful range-trading slightly lower.

Futures trod familiar paths in quiet afternoon turnover, with June Treasury bond futures observing a daily range just inside Monday's boundaries as traders turned increasingly shy ahead of next week's Federal Open Market Committee meeting.
Nearby T-bonds set a high Tuesday at 108-30/32, just below Monday's overall high of 108-31/32, and a low at 108-08/32, slightly above Monday's price trough at 108-07/32.
The market showed muted response when talk circulated of a 0.8 percent rise in weekly Redbook retail sales.
Some brokers expected more uninspired range-trading until the March 25 FOMC meeting, with even Wednesday's February consumer price index figures not expected to jolt the market.
CPI is expected to rise 0.2 percent overall and in core.
"I think the market is anticipating a rate hike," said one T-bond futures broker. "The Street is trying to play from the short side and occasionally has to scramble (to cover.)"
He said he doubted CPI would provoke much response, given that inflation has remained under control for many months.
"I really wouldn't look for major price action either way in front of FOMC next week," he added.

June Treasury bond futures early on showed more resilience than expected after February U.S. housing starts jumped 12.2 percent to an annual 1.528 million units versus forecasts for a 6.9 percent rise to 1.45 million units.
The contract clawed its way above Monday's pit-sesssion high and settlement at 108-24/32 after the housing starts figures but stalled at 108-30/32.
It drifted inside a tight range for the balance of Tuesday's pit session.

At settlement, June T-bonds fell 03/32 to 108-21/32, 10-year T-notes ended off 02/32 at 106-20/32, munis ended up 07/32 at 113-02/32, and September Eurodollars were down 0.01 at 93.90. ((Derivatives desk 312-408-8750))E-mail derivatives@reuters.com
